answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20, read-only report via `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>`; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

RECORDS & ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 of them above the completeness magnitude Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated probability):
  b     Sigma     P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0   -5.449    0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73  -5.319    0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65  -5.281    0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is the upper bound, not the calibrated estimate):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based P(Mw >= 5.5) is at most ~1.5e-2 per year (b=0.65 scenario) and as low as ~1.2e-4 per year (b=1.0), while the DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr over-counts because it treats all 34 above-Mc DAS detections as catalogue-equivalent events with uncalibrated magnitudes. A Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event is therefore unlikely by the calibrated estimate, with the DAS number serving only as a conservative ceiling.
